name: MonarchSortableGrid
title: SortableGrid
wrapsNative: LazyVGrid with draggable(_:) and dropDestination(for:action:isTargeted:) on each tile, MonarchDragHandle with accessibility actions, AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
summary: Tiles that people reorder in two dimensions by dragging, or one place or one row at a time with accessibility actions, with each move announced.
whenToUse: For a dashboard of widgets, a photo or card board, or any grid whose order the person arranges.
whenNotToUse: For a single column of rows, use a List with onMove(perform:) (see reorderable-list). For moving items between groups, use a Kanban board.
api: init(_ items: Binding<[Item]>, itemLabel: KeyPath<Item, String>, columns: Int? = nil, minimumItemWidth: CGFloat? = nil, isItemDisabled: ((Item) -> Bool)? = nil, labels: MonarchSortableGridLabels = MonarchSortableGridLabels(), onReorder: (@MainActor (_ from: Int, _ to: Int) -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Item, MonarchSortableGridItemState) -> Content)
struct MonarchSortableGridItemState { let index: Int; let isDropTarget: Bool; let isDisabled: Bool }
struct MonarchSortableGridLabels { var handle: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var moved, dropped: (@Sendable (String, Int, Int) -> String)?; var actions: [MonarchDragHandleDirection: String] }

options.name: items
options.description: The items in order. Item is Identifiable. The grid writes the new order after each move.

options.name: itemLabel
options.description: The plain-text name of an item, used in the handle's name and the announcements.

options.name: columns
options.description: A fixed number of columns. Without it, as many columns of minimumItemWidth as fit.

options.name: minimumItemWidth
options.description: The smallest tile width for adaptive columns, scaled with Dynamic Type.

options.name: isItemDisabled
options.description: Items that cannot be moved. Other items can still move past them.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the handle name, the two announcements and the move action names.

options.name: onReorder
options.description: Called after each finished move with the old and the new index, after items is updated.

options.name: content
options.description: Draws a tile. The state gives the index, whether a drag is over it and whether it is disabled.

states.name: drop target
states.description: While a dragged tile is over a tile, that tile has an accent outline and its state has isDropTarget.

states.name: disabled item
states.description: Not draggable; its handle is drawn in the disabled colour and has no actions.

states.name: disabled grid
states.description: With .disabled(true) no tile can be dragged or moved.

appearance: The grid draws only the handle in each tile's top trailing corner (muted grip, disabled colour when locked) and a strong-accent outline around the tile a drag is over. The tiles are the app's own views.
platformNotes: The web grid follows the pointer and slides the other tiles out of the way while dragging; on iOS the system drag shows a lifted preview and the order changes on drop. The web picks up a tile with Space and moves it with the arrow keys; on iOS each handle offers named actions (Move up, Move down, Move backward, Move forward) to VoiceOver, Switch Control and Full Keyboard Access. The web's uncontrolled defaultItems is not offered: the order is always a binding. The default minimum tile width is 160 points instead of the web's 12rem, so a phone shows two columns.
accessibility: Each tile has a drag handle named Reorder and the item's name, with move actions for each direction that the column count allows (up and down only in one column).
After a move with an action the new position is announced: "Design review moved to position 3 of 8."; after a drop: "Design review dropped at position 3 of 8."
Backward and forward follow reading order, so they are mirrored in right-to-left layouts with the grid.
The drop target is shown by an outline, not by colour alone.
The handle keeps a 44 by 44 point touch target; adaptive columns become fewer and wider at larger text sizes.
edgeCases: Drops of text from another grid or another app are ignored: the payload carries the grid's own id.
An action that would move a tile past the first or last place, or above the first row, does nothing.
An empty items array draws nothing.
Tiles in the same row take the height the grid gives them; give tiles a minimum height when they should line up.

examples.title: Drag or keyboard in two dimensions
examples.webExample: Drag or keyboard in two dimensions
examples.template:
MonarchSortableGrid($shortcuts, itemLabel: \.name, minimumItemWidth: {{minItemWidth}} * 16) { shortcut, _ in
    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
        Text(shortcut.name).monarchTextStyle(.bodyStrong)
        Text(shortcut.detail).monarchTextStyle(.caption)
    }
    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
    .padding(.vertical, theme.spacing.space3)
    .padding(.leading, 40)
    .padding(.trailing, theme.spacing.space3)
    .background(theme.colors.bgSurface, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: MonarchTokens.Radius.lg, style: .continuous))
    .overlay(
        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: MonarchTokens.Radius.lg, style: .continuous)
            .strokeBorder(theme.colors.borderSubtle)
    )
}
.monarchSortableGridHandle(.leading)
.accessibilityLabel({{label}})
examples.code:
MonarchSortableGrid($shortcuts, itemLabel: \.name, minimumItemWidth: 10 * 16) { shortcut, _ in
    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
        Text(shortcut.name).monarchTextStyle(.bodyStrong)
        Text(shortcut.detail).monarchTextStyle(.caption)
    }
    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
    .padding(.vertical, theme.spacing.space3)
    .padding(.leading, 40)
    .padding(.trailing, theme.spacing.space3)
    .background(theme.colors.bgSurface, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: MonarchTokens.Radius.lg, style: .continuous))
    .overlay(
        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: MonarchTokens.Radius.lg, style: .continuous)
            .strokeBorder(theme.colors.borderSubtle)
    )
}
.monarchSortableGridHandle(.leading)
.accessibilityLabel("Shortcuts")
